- [Features](#features)
- [Installation](#installation)
- [How to use Tokei](#how-to-use-tokei)

- [Supported Languages](#supported-languages)
- [Common Issues](#common-issues)
- [Copyright and License](#copyright-and-license)

## Features

- Tokei is **very fast**, and is able to count millions of lines of code in seconds.

- Tokei is **accurate**, Tokei correctly handles multi line comments,
  nested comments, and not counting comments that are in strings. Providing an
  accurate code statistics.

- Tokei has huge range of languages, supporting over **150** languages, and
  their various extensions.

- Tokei can output in multiple formats (**CBOR**, **JSON**, **YAML**)
  allowing Tokei's output to be easily stored, and reused. These can also be
  reused in tokei combining a previous run's statistics with another set.

- Tokei is available on **Mac**, **Linux**, and **Windows**.

- Tokei comes with and without color. Set the env variable NO_COLOR to 1, and
  it'll be black and white.

## Installation

### Package Managers

#### Unix
```console
# Alpine Linux (since 3.13)
apk add tokei
# Arch Linux
pacman -S tokei
# Conda
conda install -c conda-forge tokei
# Fedora
sudo dnf install tokei
# FreeBSD
pkg install tokei
# NetBSD
pkgin install tokei
# Nix/NixOS
nix-env -i tokei
# OpenSUSE
sudo zypper install tokei
# Void Linux
sudo xbps-install tokei
```

#### macOS
```console
# Homebrew
brew install tokei
# MacPorts
sudo port selfupdate
sudo port install tokei
```

#### Windows
```console
# Winget
winget install XAMPPRocky.tokei
# Scoop
scoop install tokei
```

### Manual

You can download prebuilt binaries in the releases section.

## How to use Tokei

#### Basic usage

This is the basic way to use tokei. Which will report on the code in `./foo`
and all subfolders.

```shell
$ tokei ./foo
```

#### Multiple folders
To have tokei report on multiple folders in the same call, simply add all the
folders you'd like tokei to examine.

```shell
$ tokei ./foo ./bar ./baz
```

#### Excluding folders
Tokei will respect all `.gitignore` and `.ignore` files, and you can use
the `--exclude` option to exclude any additional files. The `--exclude` flag has
the same semantics as `.gitignore`.

```shell
$ tokei ./foo --exclude *.rs
```

Paths to exclude can also be listed in a `.tokeignore` file, using the same
syntax as .gitignore files.

#### Sorting output
By default tokei sorts alphabetically by language name, however using `--sort`
tokei can also sort by any of the columns.

`blanks, code, comments, lines`

```shell
$ tokei ./foo --sort code
```

#### Outputting file statistics

```
        --no-ignore-dot       Don't respect .ignore and .tokeignore files, including those in parent directories.

    -e, --exclude <exclude>...    Ignore all files & directories matching the pattern.
    -i, --input <file_input>      Gives statistics from a previous tokei run. Can be given a file path, or "stdin" to

    -o, --output <output>         Outputs Tokei in a specific format. Compile with additional features for more format
                                  support. [possible values: cbor, json, yaml]
    -s, --sort <sort>             Sort languages based on column [possible values: files, lines, blanks, code, comments]
    -t, --type <types>            Filters output by language type, separated by a comma. i.e. -t=Rust,Markdown

ARGS:
    <input>...    The path(s) to the file or directory to be counted.
```

## Features

- Tokei is **very fast**, and is able to count millions of lines of code in seconds.

- Tokei is **accurate**, Tokei correctly handles multi line comments,
  nested comments, and not counting comments that are in strings. Providing an
  accurate code statistics.

- Tokei has huge range of languages, supporting over **150** languages, and
  their various extensions.

- Tokei can output in multiple formats (**CBOR**, **JSON**, **YAML**)
  allowing Tokei's output to be easily stored, and reused. These can also be
  reused in tokei combining a previous run's statistics with another set.

- Tokei is available on **Mac**, **Linux**, and **Windows**.

- Tokei comes with and without color. Set the env variable NO_COLOR to 1, and
  it'll be black and white.

## Installation

### Package Managers

#### Unix
```console
# Alpine Linux (since 3.13)
apk add tokei
# Arch Linux
pacman -S tokei
# Conda
conda install -c conda-forge tokei
# Fedora
sudo dnf install tokei
# FreeBSD
pkg install tokei
# NetBSD
pkgin install tokei
# Nix/NixOS
nix-env -i tokei
# OpenSUSE
sudo zypper install tokei
# Void Linux
sudo xbps-install tokei
```

#### macOS
```console
# Homebrew
brew install tokei
# MacPorts
sudo port selfupdate
sudo port install tokei
```

#### Windows
```console
# Winget
winget install XAMPPRocky.tokei
# Scoop
scoop install tokei
```

### Manual

You can download prebuilt binaries in the releases section.

## How to use Tokei

#### Basic usage

This is the basic way to use tokei. Which will report on the code in `./foo`
and all subfolders.

```shell
$ tokei ./foo
```

#### Multiple folders
To have tokei report on multiple folders in the same call, simply add all the
folders you'd like tokei to examine.

```shell
$ tokei ./foo ./bar ./baz
```

#### Excluding folders
Tokei will respect all `.gitignore` and `.ignore` files, and you can use
the `--exclude` option to exclude any additional files. The `--exclude` flag has
the same semantics as `.gitignore`.

```shell
$ tokei ./foo --exclude *.rs
```

Paths to exclude can also be listed in a `.tokeignore` file, using the same
syntax as .gitignore files.

#### Sorting output
By default tokei sorts alphabetically by language name, however using `--sort`
tokei can also sort by any of the columns.

`blanks, code, comments, lines`

```shell
$ tokei ./foo --sort code
```

#### Outputting file statistics
By default tokei only outputs the total of the languages, and using `--files`
flag tokei can also output individual file statistics.

```shell
$ tokei ./foo --files
```

#### Outputting into different formats
Tokei normally outputs into a nice human readable format designed for terminals.
There is also using the `--output` option various other formats that are more
useful for bringing the data into another program.

**Currently supported formats**
- JSON `--output json`
- YAML `--o

import subprocess, os, pty, fcntl, termios, struct
def run_pty(args, cols=100, env_extra=None):
    master, slave = pty.openpty()
    fcntl.ioctl(slave, termios.TIOCSWINSZ, struct.pack("HHHH", 24, cols, 0,0))
    env=dict(os.environ)
    if env_extra: env.update(env_extra)
    p=subprocess.Popen(["./executable"]+args, stdout=slave, stderr=slave, stdin=slave, env=env)
    os.close(slave)
    out=b""
    while True:
        try:
            d=os.read(master, 8192)
            if not d: break
            out+=d
        except OSError:
            break
    p.wait()
    return p.returncode, out

for cols in [50,80,81,82,100,200]:
    rc,out=run_pty(["/tmp/t1"], cols=cols)
    lines=out.decode().split("\r\n")
    print("cols",cols, [len(l) for l in lines])
    # first line length stripped of ansi (no ansi there)

print(repr(out.decode()))

langs=json.load(open("/tmp/langs_parsed.json"))
results=[]
# batch by creating one dir per language? But we can place many files in one dir if extensions distinct, but multiple languages share extensions conflict (eg .m etc only one mapping anyway, language determined by extension not by list duplicate). Actually extension -> language map is function; each extension unique except dup cases where one wins. For probing each LANGUAGE we need to pick an extension that maps to it; many ext map uniquely, some ext listed for multiple langs (?) e.g. "e" Specman e and Phix both e - extension mapping picks one? Earlier test a.e? Need check. Likewise "inc", "x", etc.
# Instead batch per language using its first extension and a directory with one file a.<ext> - invoking per language 331 times fine.
for name, exts_str in langs:
    if exts_str=="<None>":
        continue
    exts=[e.strip() for e in exts_str.split(",")]
    ext=exts[0]
    d="/tmp/tprobe"; shutil.rmtree(d,ignore_errors=True); os.makedirs(d)
    p=os.path.join(d,f"a.{ext}")
    try:
        open(p,"w",encoding="utf8").write("hello world\n\nsecond line\n")
    except Exception as e:
        results.append((name,ext,f"err {e}")); continue
    r=subprocess.run([EXE,"-o","json",p],capture_output=True,text=True)
    try:
        jd=json.loads(r.stdout)
        keys=[k for k in jd if k!="Total"]
        if not keys:
            results.append((name,ext,"NONE")); continue
        k=keys[0]
        s=jd[k]["reports"][0]["stats"]
        results.append((name,ext,k,s["code"],s["comments"],s["blanks"], list(s["blobs"].keys())))
    except Exception as e:
        results.append((name,ext,f"parse {e} {r.stdout[:100]} {r.stderr[:100]}"))
for r in results:
    print(r)
json.dump(results,open("/tmp/probe_plain.json","w"),ensure_ascii=False,indent=1)


#### Outputting into different formats
Tokei normally outputs into a nice human readable format designed for terminals.
There is also using the `--output` option various other formats that are more
useful for bringing the data into another program.

**Currently supported formats**
- JSON `--output json`
- YAML `--output yaml`
- CBOR `--output cbor`

```shell
$ tokei ./foo --output json
```

#### Reading in stored formats
Tokei can also take in the outputted formats added in the previous results to its
current run. Tokei can take either a path to a file, the format passed in as a
value to the option, or from stdin.

```shell
$ tokei ./foo --input ./stats.json
```

## Options

import pty, os, subprocess, fcntl, termios, struct, sys
EXE="/workspace/executable"
def run(stdin_is_tty,stdout_is_tty,stderr_is_tty,cols=120,args=["--files","/tmp/t1"]):
    master,slave=pty.openpty(); fcntl.ioctl(slave,termios.TIOCSWINSZ,struct.pack("HHHH",24,cols,0,0))
    # stdin from devnull or slave, etc.
    p=subprocess.Popen([EXE]+args, stdin=slave if stdin_is_tty else subprocess.DEVNULL, stdout=slave if stdout_is_tty else subprocess.PIPE, stderr=slave if stderr_is_tty else subprocess.PIPE)
    os.close(slave)
    out_tty=b""
    # If stdout is piped, read pipe after close? Need avoid deadlock: main output ties
    if stdout_is_tty:
        while True:
            try:
                d=os.read(master,8192)
                if not d: break
                out_tty+=d
            except: break
        p.wait(); print(stdin_is_tty,stdout_is_tty,stderr_is_tty,"ttyfirstlen",len(out_tty.decode(errors='ignore').replace("\r","").splitlines()[0]) if out_tty else None)
    else:
        out,err=p.communicate(); print(stdin_is_tty,stdout_is_tty,stderr_is_tty,"pipefirstlen",len(out.decode().splitlines()[0]))
for combo in [(True,True,True),(False,True,False),(True,False,False),(False,False,True),(True,False,True)]:
    run(*combo)
# for languages
for combo in [(False,True,False),(True,False,False)]:
    run(*combo, args=["-l"])

import subprocess,json,os,shutil,re
langs=json.load(open("/tmp/langs_parsed.json")); variants=json.load(open("/tmp/lang_variants.json"))

for (name,exts),(_,var) in zip(langs,variants):
    vals=[]
    if exts!="<None>": vals += [e.strip() for e in exts.split(",")]
    vals += [name, name.lower(), name.replace(" ","").lower(), var, var.lower()]
    for v in vals:
        if v and "/" not in v and "\\" not in v and "\n" not in v and v not in cands:
            cands.append(v)
print("candidates",len(cands))
# env form batch
for form_idx,formname in enumerate(["env","bin","usrbin"]):
    d="/tmp/tsheb_all"; shutil.rmtree(d,ignore_errors=True); os.makedirs(d)
    for i,tok in enumerate(cands):
        # token may contain spaces or symbols; env argument will be first word (?) For our discovery keep as is (shebang token split)
        if formname=="env": content=f"#!/usr/bin/env {tok}\nhello\n"
        elif formname=="bin": content=f"#!/bin/{tok}\nhello\n"
        else: content=f"#!/usr/bin/{tok}\nhello\n"
        open(os.path.join(d,f"p{i:03d}"),"w",encoding="utf8").write(content)
    r=subprocess.run(["./executable","-o","json",d],capture_output=True,text=True,timeout=30)
    jd=json.loads(r.stdout); out={}
    for lang,data in jd.items():
      if lang=="Total": continue
      for rep in data["reports"]:
        i=int(re.search(r'p(\d{3})',rep["name"]).group(1)); out[cands[i]]=lang
    print(formname,out)
    json.dump(out,open(f"/tmp/shebang_{formname}.json","w"),ensure_ascii=False,indent=1)

import json, re
langs=json.load(open("/tmp/langs_parsed.json"))
variants=json.load(open("/tmp/lang_variants.json"))

import glob

  try:
    d=json.load(open(f)); nested.update(d)
  except: pass
quotes_probe=json.load(open('/tmp/probe_q_all.json'))

# manual overrides: name -> dict with line/block/quotes additions or replacements
# quotes entries (start,end,kind) kind N normal, V verbatim
def Q(s,e=None,k='N'): return (s,e or s,k)

manual={}
def setman(name,**kw): manual[name]=kw

# Clean false line tokens etc handled below; specific overrides
setman('hledger', line=[';','#'], block=[('comment','end comment',False)])
setman('PowerShell', block=[('<#','#>',False)])
setman('ASP.NET', block=[('<!--','-->',False),('<%--','--%>',False)])
setman('Pascal', line=['//'], block=[('{','}',True),('(*','*)',True)])
setman('FORTRAN Legacy', line=['!','*','C','c'], kind='Fortran')
setman('FORTRAN Modern', line=['!'], kind='Fortran')
setman('Markdown', kind='Markdown')
setman('Unreal Markdown', kind='UnrealMarkdown')
setman('Djot', kind='Prose')
setman('MDX', kind='Prose')
setman('Plain Text', kind='Prose')
setman('Jupyter Notebooks', kind='Jupyter')
# Known additions / fixes
add_block={
 'CoffeeScript':[('###','###',False)],
 'Lean':[('/-','-/',True),('/--','-/',True)],
 'Nim':[('#[',']#',True)],
 'Protocol Buffers':[('/*','*/',False)],
 'Cairo':[('/*','*/',False)],
 'WebGPU Shader Language':[('/*','*/',False)],
 'MoonScript':[],
 'Raku':[('=begin','=end',False)],
 'Perl':[('=pod','=cut',False),('=begin','=cut',False),('=for','=cut',False)],
 'ASN.1':[],
 'AutoHotKey':[],
 'LD Script':[],
 'OpenCL':[],
 'Poke':[],
 'SQL':[],
 'VHDL':[],
 'LiveScript':[],
 'Logtalk':[],
 'Oz':[],
 'Prolog':[],
 'Nix':[],
}
add_line={
 'CoffeeScript':['#'],
 'Lean':['--'],
 'Gwion':['//'], # probe gave #! maybe actual? check later; keep inferred too below not replace
}

triple_double = {"Python","Cython","Mojo","GDScript","Julia","Groovy","Scala","Kotlin","Swift","Java","C#","F#","Dart","Elixir","Elm","Nim","Crystal","Ren'Py","Snakemake"}
triple_single = {"Python","Cython","Mojo","GDScript","Groovy","Dart","Ren'Py","Snakemake"}

# verbatim / special quotes manually known from probing/trace and language knowledge
verbatim={
 'Rust':[Q('r#"','"#','V'),Q('r##"','"##','V'),Q('r###"','"###','V'),Q('r####"','"####','V'),Q('r#####"','"#####','V')],
 'C#':[Q('@"','"','V'),Q('$@"','"','V'),Q('@$"','"','V'),Q('"""','"""','V')],
 'F#':[Q('@"','"','V')],
 'Python':[], # raw handled as normal quote after prefix in tokei? leave
 'C++':[Q('R"(',')"','V')],
 'C++ Header':[Q('R"(',')"','V')],
 'C Header':[],
 'D':[Q('r"','"','V'),Q('`','`','V')],
 'Julia':[],
 'Go':[],
}

def clean_line(name,toks):
    out=[]
    for t in toks:
        if t=='//*':
            continue
        if t==' * ':
            t='*'
        if t.endswith('comment') and len(t)>7 and t[:-7] in ('C','c','D','d','#','//','--',';','%','*','!','"',"'",'`',':','x'):
            t=t[:-7]
        if t=='dnl ':
            t='dnl'
        if t=='rem ':
            t='rem'
        if t=='C ':
            t='C'
        if t=='c ':
            t='c'
        if t not in out:
            out.append(t)
    # Remove a token that is a superstring solely due spaces e.g. ' *' handled
    out=[t for t in out if t]
    # minimal prefix again (except keep doc tokens? no line list doesn't include doc)
    res=[]
    for t in sorted(out,key=lambda x:(len(x),x)):
        if any(t.startswith(k) for k in res):
            continue
        res.append(t)
    return res

def clean_block(name,pairs):
    out=[]
    for a,b in pairs:
        # nested lookup
        nest=False
        for row in nested.get(name,[]):
            if row[0]==[a,b]:
                nest=bool(row[3]); break
        out.append((a,b,nest))
    return out

def rust_str(s):
    return json.dumps(s,ensure_ascii=False)

entries=[]
for (name,extstr),(dname,var) in zip(langs,variants):
    assert name==dname
    spec=specs.get(name,{})
    line=clean_line(name,spec.get('line',[]))
    block=clean_block(name,[tuple(x) for x in spec.get('block',[])])
    kind='Normal'
    # manual apply
    if name in manual:
        m=manual[name]
        if 'line' in m: line=m['line']
        if 'block' in m: block=m['block']
        if 'kind' in m: kind=m['kind']
    if name in add_block:
        for a,b,n in add_block[name]:
            if (a,b,n) not in block and (a,b,False) not in block and (a,b,True) not in block:
                block.append((a,b,n))
    if name in add_line:
        for t in add_line[name]:
            if t not in line: line.append(t)
    # Gwion probe line was #! - keep as is if present (manual above adds //, maybe wrong, comment out by not special)
    if name=='Gwion':
        # remove added // if we are uncertain? Let's keep both; token // plausible C-like Gwion.
        pass
    # extensions
    if extstr=='<None>':
        exts=[]
    else:
        exts=[e.strip() for e in extstr.split(',')]
    # quotes from probe
    qs=[]
    qd=quotes_probe.get(name)
    if qd:
        rows={tuple(r[0]):(r[1],r[2]) for r in qd['rows']}
        base=rows.get(('ZZ','ZZ'))
        for ch in ['"',"'",'`']:
            if rows.get((ch,ch))==(3,1):
                # exclude if ch is a line comment token (ASP/VB etc where ' is comment, probe marker weird and may still produce)
                if ch in line:
                    continue
                qs.append(Q(ch))
    # triple additions first
    special_q=[]
    if name in triple_double:
        special_q.append(Q('"""','"""','N'))
    if name in triple_single:
        special_q.append(Q("'''","'''",'N'))
    if name in verbatim:
        special_q = verbatim[name] + special_q
    # Dedupe preserve special first then qs
    allq=[]
    for q in special_q+qs:
        if q not in allq: allq.append(q)
    entries.append(dict(name=name,var=var,exts=exts,line=line,block=block,quotes=allq,kind=kind))

# Output Rust
out=[]
out.append("// Language definitions derived from observed behaviour of the reference executable")
out.append("// (extensions/names from --languages, comment tokens discovered by probing files).")
out.append("")
out.append("#[derive(Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq, PartialOrd, Ord, Hash, Debug)]")
out.append("pub enum LanguageType {")
for e in entries:
    out.append(f"    {e['var']},")
out.append("}")
out.append("")
out.append("pub static LANGUAGE_SPECS: &[LanguageSpec] = &[")
for e in entries:
    exts=', '.join(rust_str(x) for x in e['exts'])
    line=', '.join(rust_str(x) for x in e['line'])
    block=', '.join(f"BlockComment {{ start: {rust_str(a)}, end: {rust_str(b)}, nested: {str(n).lower()} }}" for a,b,n in e['block'])
    qs=', '.join(f"Quote {{ start: {rust_str(a)}, end: {rust_str(b)}, kind: QuoteKind::{'Verbatim' if k=='V' else 'Normal'} }}" for a,b,k in e['quotes'])
    out.append("    LanguageSpec {")
    out.append(f"        name: {rust_str(e['name'])},")
    out.append(f"        extensions: &[{exts}],")
    out.append(f"        line_comments: &[{line}],")
    out.append(f"        block_comments: &[{block}],")
    out.append(f"        quotes: &[{qs}],")
    out.append(f"        kind: SpecKind::{e['kind']},")
    out.append("    },")
out.append("];")
open("src/languages_data.rs","w").write("\n".join(out)+"\n")
print("wrote",len(entries))
PY
python3 /tmp/gen_languages.py
wc -l src/languages_data.rs; sed -n '1,80p' src/languages_data.rs"}

        }
        // Summary row for this language.

            out,
            "{}",
            summary_row(
                lang_type.name(),
                name_width,
                Some(lang.files()),
                lang.lines(),
                lang.code,
                lang.comments,
                lang.blanks,
                cli,
                lang.inaccurate,
                true,
                false,
            )
        )?;

        let show_children = !cli.compact && !lang.children.is_empty();
        if show_children {
            for (child_type, reports) in &lang.children {
                let child = Language::summarise(reports);
                let (clines, ccode, ccomments, cblanks) = child.total();
                writeln!(
                    out,
                    "{}",
                    child_row(
                        child_type.name(),
                        name_width,

                        clines,
                        ccode,
                        ccomments,
                        cblanks,
                        cli,

                    tcode,
                    tcomments,
                    tblanks,
                    cli,
                    false,
                    false,
                    false,

                            false,
                            false,
                            false,
                        )
                    )?;
                }

        }

            name_width,

            cli,
            total_lang.inaccurate,
            true,
            true,
        )
    )?;
    writeln!(out, "{heavy}")?;
    out.flush()

check('dir.py',['/tmp/cmpspecial/dir.py'])
